negative_findings.description: No public Temenos or Oracle FLEXCUBE implementation announcement naming a Ukrainian bank or a Ukraine-based implementation partner surfaced in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only generic vendor comparison and aggregator pages; no Ukraine-specific customer story, partner listing or go-live release was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the Tier-1 Western core-banking vendors have little publicly announced Ukrainian install base, so the indirect route for private banks must lean on domestic vendors (CS Ltd, UNITY-BARS, ProFIX) and processors (UPC, ProCard, TAS-Link) rather than the global names in the cell brief.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated OpenWay case study for a Ukrainian bank was located; the only Ukraine link found was a statement that Way4 project teams span 15+ countries including Ukraine.
negative_findings.result_summary: OpenWay customer stories found covered B1NK, Capital Bank and RPC, none Ukrainian.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: OpenWay's Ukraine relevance may be as an employer/delivery location rather than as a supplier to Ukrainian banks — which changes what to monitor (careers and delivery-centre news, not customer stories).

negative_findings.description: The clearest BPC/Ukraine client evidence found (Visa payWave go-live at Credit Dnepr Bank on SmartVista) is an old release republished by trade press, not current BPC newsroom content.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Current BPC activity in Ukraine is unconfirmed; the source is worth tracking but the install-base inference from that release must not be treated as current-state.

negative_findings.description: No established Ukrainian-language term set was found for 'partner-hire announcement' / 'client-side project sponsor' as a discoverable phrase.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future local-language queries should target concrete artefacts (назва банку + впровадження, кейс, реліз, пресцентр) rather than the abstract concept, or recall will stay low.

brief: For Ukraine, the private-bank indirect route runs mainly through domestic suppliers rather than the global names in the cell brief: CS Ltd (АБС Б2, iFOBS), UNITY-BARS (ABS BARS) and ProFIX on the core/back-office side, and UPC, ProCard, TAS-Link and UkrCard on the card/processing side, all of which publish client-naming project news in Ukrainian. Searches produced no Ukraine-specific customer story for Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE or OpenWay, and the only BPC/Ukraine trace found is an older SmartVista go-live at Credit Dnepr Bank republished by trade press — so the multinational branch of this cell is thin and should be monitored opportunistically rather than as a core feed. The strongest recurring signals are vendor press centres, Ukrainian fintech trade media (PSM7, Fintech Insider UA, Banker.ua) that publish actor-mapping market overviews, and hiring instruments (jobs.dou.ua company pages, SoftServe's country-filtered vacancy feed, IT Ukraine Association headcount rankings) that quantify delivery-centre expansion. NBU newsroom items — operator designations, open banking from 1 Aug 2025, ISO 20022 — provide the timing skeleton that explains when vendor-side activity should spike.
